title: Honor Retry-After when retrying deliveries
body:
Receivers that rate-limit us or are briefly down send a `Retry-After` header, usually with `429` or `503`. We ignore it and schedule the retry on our own backoff, which usually lands inside their limit window again.

The worker now schedules the next attempt as far out as `Retry-After` asks, in either seconds or HTTP-date form, on any error response that carries it, and falls back to the existing backoff when the header is missing or unreadable. The delay is capped at `MAX_DELAY` (60s), like the backoff. That covers every value receivers send today: over the last 30 days, the `Retry-After` values in our delivery logs ranged from 1s to 30s, so the cap only guards against a misconfigured receiver pushing its retries out for hours.

Tested with `pytest`; the new cases are in `tests/test_backoff.py` and `tests/test_worker.py`.
